what: Southern Company is a regulated electric and gas utility in the southeastern United States. Alabama Power, Georgia Power and Mississippi Power supply electricity to homes and businesses, and Southern Company Gas distributes natural gas.
customers: Households, businesses and industrial users in Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi and gas customers in several states.
money: electricity generation, transmission and retail supply in the Southeast
wholesale generation sold under long-term contracts
moat: A legal monopoly in its service territory, with prices set by state regulators to cover costs plus an allowed return on the money it invests.
risks: Debt of more than $70 billion makes it sensitive to interest rates
State regulators decide whether it can recover its investments through bills
Large construction projects have run badly over budget before, as at Plant Vogtle
Storms and extreme weather damage the network
opportunities: Data centre construction in Georgia is driving the fastest electricity demand growth in decades
Every approved investment in the grid raises the earnings base it is allowed to charge for
A dividend raised for more than two decades supports the shares
watch: Approved rate cases and the size of the capital plan, which together set earnings growth.
